Thanks again for today’s demo and the clear explanation of Redwood’s routing and fallbacks. As promised, I wanted to consolidate the technical asks from our engineering team so we can get a tighter qualification: 

- We need a short written summary of recommended deployment topology for a VPC/private deployment (we handle PHI).
- Expected baseline throughput for our mid-sized workload (see quick numbers below) and what dedicated capacity you’d recommend.
- Typical latency P95/P99 targets when using an ~70B family open model and streaming vs. non-streaming modes.
- Any SOC 2 / KMS evidence you can surface and the procurement path for Private.

Quick context from our side (from call): 8k DAU, peak concurrency ~45 active requests, median prompt length ~70 tokens, average generation ~120 tokens. We’ll attach a simple SLO matrix that the security team asked us to fill — it has placeholders for retention and audit logs.

Can you send a concise technical recap and next steps for a short POC (2 weeks) we can run inside our VPC? Ideally we’ll get a checklist we can hand to our infra team.

Appreciate it — Emily

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the details and the SLO matrix. Below is a focused technical recap from our side plus an ops-level plan that maps to your constraints (PHI, VPC). I’ve kept this intentionally short — Karthik (engineer) and Mina (security) are cc’d for any deep dives and SOC/KMS specifics.

1) Pain points & goals we heard
- PHI + compliance: data must remain inside your VPC and meet SOC2/KMS auditability.
- Tight P95 latency for short form completions (chat-like UX) and predictable burst handling during concurrency spikes.
- Minimize per-token cost while keeping quality stable.

2) Recommended deployment topology (initial POC)
- Mode: Redwood Private (VPC deployment) with a customer-facing control plane and on-prem/private data path.
- Baseline cluster: 2 shards of 4 x A100-80GB (or equivalent) per shard for redundancy — ~8 GPUs reserved for POC.
- Replication: 1 primary + 1 standby per shard for fast failover.
- Networking: VPC peering + NAT for control-plane telemetry; we’ll provide an Ops runbook for required firewall rules and ports.
- Fallbacks: model routing policy to a smaller 13B quantized variant for very tight latency SLOs.

3) Model & inference profile
- Recommended model family: open-llama-3-70b (quantized int8) for fidelity; open-llama-3-13b quantized as a latency fallback.
- Serving config: streaming enabled for UX, delta-streaming to reduce tail latency.
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts — big wins for your median prompt patterns.

4) SLO guidance & capacity estimate (POC sizing)
- Target SLOs to test in POC: P95 <= 300ms for streaming token events (note: end-to-end P95 may be higher depending on client aggregation); P99 <= 850ms.
- Conservative throughput estimate (typical small-to-mid GA runs): with 8 x A100s and batching tuned for ~16 concurrent requests, expect ~200–350 qps for short-gen workloads (~120 gen tokens average) using the 70B int8 path.
- If you need consistent sub-200ms P95, route a percentage of traffic to the 13B fallback layer and reserve burst capacity + autoscale slots.

5) Data / security notes
- We support customer-managed KMS + HSM integration; Mina will attach the SOC2 evidence and an onboarding checklist.
- Audit logs: request/response hashes and token usage can be logged to your audit sink in near-real-time (configurable retention).

6) Next steps / proposal for the POC
- Deliverable: 2-week proof-of-performance inside your VPC: baseline runbook, test dataset, telemetry collection, and a short scorecard comparing latency/throughput vs target SLOs.
- Action items I’ll take: provide the detailed POC runbook, wiring diagram, and a short bill-of-materials for the 8-GPU reservation.
- Action items for you: confirm a POC start week and provide a small representative traffic sample (1–2 days of request logs) and the completed SLO matrix.

I’ll follow up with the runbook and BOM by end of day tomorrow. Karthik, Mina — can you add any infrastructure or security caveats I should include?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com]

Emily / Jasmine — quick engineering notes to supplement Jasmine’s recap:

- Batching & batching window: for your median gen sizes (120 tokens) we recommend adaptive batching with a 12–18ms max wait window; this balances latency and throughput.
- KV cache: if you have repeated prompt prefixes (e.g., system prompt + user context), enable per-user prefix caching — expect 20–40% token compute savings on repeat flows.
- Tokenization overhead: anticipate ~1.02x tokens on LLM tokenization for your english-heavy prompts — include that in telemetry.
- Streaming considerations: P95 for the first token is typically dominated by decoder latency; for streaming UX, measure both "first-token P95" and "completion P95". For our 70B quantized path, first-token P95 target ~180–240ms with the config Jasmine suggested.
- Bench numbers we can reproduce in POC: on our infra template, 4xA100 (80GB) can handle ~90–120 qps for 70B int8 w/ 120 token decode when aggressively batched; doubling to 8 GPUs gives roughly linear gains after accounting for network/replication overhead.

Red flags to watch during POC:
- Long-tail concurrency spikes (e.g., sudden 200+ concurrent) will require burst provisioning — test canary traffic patterns to validate autoscaler triggers.
- If you use long context windows (>2k tokens), memory and KV strategy will materially change sizing.

I’ll include a small config snippet in the POC runbook showing the batching knobs and cache TTLs.

— Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

- SOC2: attached is our SOC2 Type II summary + control mappings (redacted). We support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS or on-prem HSM; HSM integration will require a short network setup in the POC runbook.
- Audit trails: we can push hashed request/response audit records to your audit sink with configurable retention; retention policies are enforced via the control plane you manage inside the VPC.
- Onboarding checklist: I’ve attached a POC checklist that includes firewall rules, required IAM roles, and a minimum telemetry sample schema we need.

POC plan (timeline suggestion)
- Week 0 (prep): access & VPC peering, baseline infra provisioning (we supply Terraform templates), test dataset upload.
- Week 1 (run): baseline runs, smoke tests, telemetry capture.
- Week 2 (validation): SLO runbook execution, failure injection (optional), final scorecard + recommendations.

Proposed kickoff: June 4th (Mon) — if that looks good we’ll reserve a small dedicated engineering window and send calendar invites.

I’ll drop the SOC2 and POC checklist to the Drive link Jasmine listed.
